# Search performance diagnosis: https://app.example.test

## Bottom line

There is no usable diagnosis available right now. The only connected Search Console export is for a different property (`https://www.example.test`), and the alleged drop rests on a 5-to-4 click change with no completed comparable window and no conversion data. Nothing in the available evidence supports a material incident on `app.example.test`.

## Evidence boundary

- Target property: `https://app.example.test` (distinct host).
- Connected export: `https://www.example.test`. A different hostname is a neighboring property, not a fallback for the app host. Its data cannot be substituted, filtered, or extrapolated to describe `app.example.test`.
- Ownership/verification state, API consent, and a successful scoped query for the app host are separate states. None of them is established here.
- No messages to others are authorized, so this stays in chat as a report to you only.

## What the "20% drop" claim actually is

- 5 clicks to 4 clicks is a one-click change. Reporting it as 20% is arithmetically true and diagnostically empty at that volume.
- No completed matching comparison window is available, so the two figures are not known to cover equal-length, equal-filter, equal-freshness periods.
- At this volume, normal variance, reporting lag, weekday/seasonality effects, and a single visitor's behavior are all sufficient explanations. There is no baseline from which a threshold could be set, and no universal 20% alert threshold applies.
- Conclusion: `No data (no completed comparable window)` for whether a real change occurred. Do not treat this as a confirmed decline.

## What is unknown

| Question | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Is `app.example.test` verified with scoped Search Console data access? | No data | Only the `www` property is connected |
| Search clicks/impressions for the app host over comparable windows | No data | Property not connected; the `www` export is a different property |
| Whether the 5 to 4 change is real, seasonal, or lag artifact | No data | No completed matching comparison window |
| Brand vs non-brand, page-group, country, device segmentation | No data | Depends on scoped app-property access |
| Google generative AI visibility for the app host | Not measured | Report provides impressions by page, country, device, date only; no AI clicks or CTR exist to read, and access to the app property is unconfirmed |
| Bing/Copilot citations for the app host | Not measured | Bing AI Performance provides citations and cited pages; app-property access unconfirmed. Citations are not rankings or referral sessions |
| Whether discovery produced qualified outcomes | No data | No conversion data available; conversion event, hostname/path filter, and attribution window are all unverified |
| Whether any indexing or delivery defect exists on the app host | Not measured | No crawl or public probe has been run in this task |

Also unknown by definition, and not interchangeable even once measured: search impressions, Google AI impressions, Bing citations, vendor prompt demand estimates, and analytics sessions. Vendor prompt volumes are demand estimates for a topic, not this site's share of visibility.

## Next measurement steps, smallest first

1. **Establish scoped access to the app property.** Add and verify `https://app.example.test` in Search Console as its own property (URL-prefix or domain, matching how the host is served). Verification, API consent, and a successful scoped query are three separate confirmations; report each. Preserve any existing DNS verification on the `www` property; no new meta token is required for DNS verification.
2. **Confirm whether the app host is on a shared domain path structure.** If any app content is served under a path on another host, filter that path separately rather than reading a whole-property total.
3. **Re-pull the click figures as a completed comparable window.** Once scoped access exists, compare two equal-length completed periods with matching filters, aggregation, and data freshness, and report absolute counts beside any percentage. At 4 to 5 clicks, extend the window (for example 28 days versus the prior 28 days) rather than comparing short windows.
4. **Rule out non-ranking causes before ranking causes.** Check reporting lag, weekday and seasonality effects, releases or migrations on the app host, and any tracking or property configuration change in the same window.
5. **Run public checks now, while authenticated data is unavailable.** Fetch the app host's robots file, sitemap and its listed URLs, and the response status, canonical, robots directives and server-rendered content of the main indexable routes. This can surface a blocking defect independently of Search Console and needs no vendor access.
6. **Separate AI surfaces once access exists.** Read Google generative AI performance for impressions by page, country, device and date, and Bing AI Performance for citations and cited pages. Report each engine separately with its own scope and window. Do not derive AI clicks or CTR from impression-only data.
7. **Verify conversion instrumentation before judging traffic quality.** Confirm hostname, path filter, conversion event definition and attribution window in analytics. Until then, any statement about whether SEO traffic quality changed is `No data`.

## Monitoring

The existing monitor already targets `app.example.test`. Reuse it; do not create a second owner or schedule. Keep its configured destination and notification preferences as they are. No recap or notification goes to anyone else, since no messages to others are authorized.

Once the app property has scoped access, the useful change to the existing monitor is threshold calibration: set alerting from the observed baseline volume, its normal variance, persistence across periods, and business impact. At single-digit weekly clicks, a percentage threshold will fire on noise; prefer persistence over several comparable periods plus an absolute floor, and keep actionable access or delivery failures as their own alert class. Deduplicate against the already-reported 5-to-4 item so it is not raised again unchanged.

## Verification state of this report

- Checks run in this task: none. No crawl, no fetch, no export, no query was executed.
- Everything above is derived from the stated evidence boundary and tool capability snapshot.
- Strongest state actually verified: the connected export belongs to a different property than the one under diagnosis. Nothing about `app.example.test` performance is measured.
